characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: The Technical Feasibility Strategy lever controls the project's ability to demonstrate technical feasibility, which in turn impacts policy. The immediate consequence of this lever is the creation of demonstrators that showcase secure authentication methods such as FIDO2 on mainstream Android devices or browser-based fallbacks. This leads to a 15% increase in policy traction due to concrete evidence and enhances credibility in procurement negotiations at the systemic level. Strategically, this lever ensures that the project's technical capabilities are aligned with its broader goals of reducing dependency on foreign technology suppliers.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever has strong synergy with the Coalition Building Strategy (1731ad9a-c471-40de-9b90-12f23721aebd) as a well-built coalition can amplify the impact of technical feasibility demonstrations. The Technical Feasibility Strategy also has synergy with the Procurement Influence Strategy (f1c0d856-0cfc-4def-ab68-c58bb8b17551), as demonstrating technical feasibility is crucial for influencing procurement decisions.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This lever has a conflict with the Focus on Demonstrator Efforts on a Single, Highly Secure Authentication Method option within the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474), as it might limit the scope of demonstrator efforts and overlook potential benefits from exploring multiple authentication methods. Additionally, this lever has a conflict with the Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach within the Technical Feasibility Strategy (bd43cd39-f2f0-4358-9f5b-e4dbfdccc474), as it might lead to budget overruns or inefficient resource allocation.
